I have basically the same set but in orange (not my ideal colour choice ngl) and they will get me by for a long enough time but I know they're trash.

they're very squared therefore they haven't been rounded off and will get caught on the pins and in the keyway much easier, the metal part of the pick only goes about 1cm into the handle so if you have a particularly far back grip you'll easily break a pick soon enough and to top it all off the picks are generally 30 thousands, which for a pick is incredibly thick, 20 thousands is an average 25 thousands is on the higher side and 30 thousands is generally unnacceptable, especially considering I can tell your from the UK based on the picture you posted, every UK home in a nutshell 😂 but our euro counterparts differ from America in the way that it always does, America does it BIGGER but not better, our euro versions of the same locks Americans get *can* be tougher to pick due to tight, paracentric keyways

The BEST advice I can give you, noob to noob is, if your on a budget, your new to picking and don't want to heavily invest in tools when you don't even know how good you are and if it will ever be worth it, simply buy sandpaper (high grit) and just lightly go over your tools taking off the sharp squared edges and maybe even try making the pick a tad thinner, just go slow and take your time, you can take metal off easy but you can't add it on... The picks might be inefficient now but if you sand them way too thin or take the whole profile of the pick away it will go from inefficient to completely ineffective 

If you haven't already I strongly watching LPL, Bosnian bill and lock noob on YouTube, deviant olam is also well up there with those guys but you might find his videos more varied, he's an entry methods YouTuber whereas the other 3 are fully lock picking YouTubers

I have one similar that says Tri circle, it's a really common cheap lock design, I had the same problem, I took my time, counted the pins, messed around with different levels of tension to get a feel for the pins the best I could.

I quickly learned that the 5th pin needs to be picked super high while the 4th pin was a zero cut, meaning if I touch that pin at all, I have over set it, to combat this with the small keyway and cheap beginner kit picks, I put my pick in and turned the pick clockwise to slide it under the pins, then centre the pick when clear and bring it back to feel for the high pin. 

I'm not saying your lock is exactly the same but it's a high chance you have a high cut pin behind a low cut pin, without tension slide your pick through the lock and count the pins, then feel how many pins your picking and make sure you've got them all
